name: git-tree
description: A SourceTree- and GitLens-class Git client for VS Code with first-class multi-repo support.
author: Javian Picardo Group Inc

gitTree.git.path.description: Absolute path to the git executable. Leave empty to auto-detect.

gitTree.git.maxConcurrentProcesses.description: Maximum concurrent git processes across all repositories. 0 = auto (min(8, cpuCount)).

gitTree.discovery.maxDepth.description: How many directory levels below each workspace folder to scan for repositories.

gitTree.discovery.excludeGlobs.description: Additional directory names to skip while scanning for repositories.

gitTree.bitbucket.oauthConsumerKey.markdownDescription: Key of your own Bitbucket OAuth consumer, for browser sign-in. Leave empty to use the one built into Git Tree. Callback URL to register: `http://127.0.0.1:47231/oauth/bitbucket`.

gitTree.bitbucket.oauthConsumerSecret.markdownDescription: Secret of your own Bitbucket OAuth consumer (used together with the key above). Stored in plain text in settings — prefer the built-in consumer unless your workspace requires its own.

gitTree.gitlab.oauthApplicationId.markdownDescription: Application ID of your own GitLab.com application, for browser sign-in. Leave empty to use the one built into Git Tree. Register it as non-confidential with scope `api` and redirect URI `vscode://javian-picardo-group-inc.git-tree/oauth/gitlab`.

gitTree.followActiveEditor.description: Make the repository owning the active editor the active repository.

gitTree.autoRefresh.description: Automatically refresh repositories when their files change. When off, refresh manually with the Refresh Repositories command.

gitTree.accentColor.description: Accent color for the GitTree interface.

gitTree.graph.density.description: Row density of the commit graph.

gitTree.ai.enabled.description: Enable AI features. Requires explicit opt-in; no AI request is ever sent in the background.

gitTree.ai.provider.description: AI backend. 'vscode-lm' uses the editor's built-in language model (no API key).

gitTree.ai.model.description: Model used when the provider is 'anthropic'.

gitTree.ai.excludeGlobs.description: Files never included in an AI request payload.

gitTree.discovery.extraPaths.markdownDescription: Extra folders to scan for repositories and worktrees, in addition to the workspace folders — useful when the workspace root is not itself a repository. `~` and `${userHome}` are expanded. Scanned to `#gitTree.discovery.maxDepth#`.

gitTree.worktrees.directory.markdownDescription: Folder new worktrees are created in. Empty means a folder beside the repository: `<repo>.worktrees` (e.g. `C:ProjectsGitTree.worktrees eature-login`). Variables: `${userHome}`, `${repoName}`, `${repoParent}`, `${repoRoot}`, `${branch}`, and a leading `~`. Without `${branch}`, the branch folder is appended. Each repository can override this in Git Tree ▸ Settings ▸ Worktrees.

gitTree.worktrees.subfolder.markdownDescription: Create worktrees in this folder **inside** the repository instead (e.g. `.worktrees`). Takes precedence over `#gitTree.worktrees.directory#`; Git Tree adds it to `.git/info/exclude` so it never shows as untracked.

gitTree.worktrees.preserveBranchHierarch.markdownDescription: Keep branch folders in worktree paths: `feature/login` → `feature/login` when on, `feature-login` when off.

enumDescriptions: Open it as a repository tab in Git Tree.
Open its folder in a new VS Code window.
Open its folder in this VS Code window.
Do not open it after creating.
gitTree.worktrees.openBehavior.description: What happens after creating a worktree, and when you double-click one in the Worktrees section.

gitTree.worktrees.preserveSubfolder.description: When opening a worktree in a VS Code window, open the same sub-folder you are in now (e.g. a package of a monorepo), falling back to the worktree root.

gitTree.worktrees.autoPull.markdownDescription: Pre-tick "Pull after creating" in the New Worktree sheet: `git pull --ff-only` in a new worktree of an existing branch with an upstream.

gitTree.worktrees.autoPush.markdownDescription: Pre-tick "Push the new branch" in the New Worktree sheet: `git push --set-upstream` after creating a new branch.

gitTree.worktrees.deleteGoneBranchOnRemo.description: Pre-tick "Also delete the branch" when removing a worktree whose branch no longer exists on the remote.

gitTree.worktrees.copyInclude.markdownDescription: Untracked or ignored files and folders to copy from the current worktree into a new one, as globs relative to the repository root, e.g. `.env`, `.env.*`, `.venv`, `docs/tmp/**`. Nothing is ever overwritten. Each repository can override this.

gitTree.worktrees.copyExclude.markdownDescription: Globs left out of the copy even when included, e.g. `**/node_modules`, `target`.

gitTree.worktrees.colorLabels.description: Show worktree colour labels: a dot in the Worktrees section and an accent on the repository tab.

enumDescriptions: Open a coloured worktree through a generated .code-workspace file (kept in Git Tree's storage, never in the repository) that tints the window's title bar.
gitTree.worktrees.titleBarTint.description: Tint the title bar of a VS Code window opened on a coloured worktree.
